where: Section 1, last paragraph, and the figure
problem: The chapter states flatly that MQTT and CoAP 'sit at the application layer'. In the four-layer IoT model used here (perception, network, middleware, application) many syllabi file MQTT, CoAP and 6LoWPAN under the network layer, because they move data rather than present it to a user. A student with a different textbook will see an apparent contradiction.
fix: Add one line: 'These are data-moving protocols that sit just above the radio link; TCP/IP-style diagrams put them at the application layer, while some IoT layer diagrams file them under the network layer. This chapter uses the TCP/IP view.'

where: Quiz Q4 and the QoS 2 row of the table
problem: The answer implies that QoS 2 gives exactly-once delivery all the way from publisher to subscriber. MQTT's exactly-once handshake works separately on each leg, publisher-to-broker and broker-to-subscriber, so it is exactly once per hop, not end-to-end across the broker.
fix: add: 'QoS 2 is exactly once between each client and the broker. The publisher must publish at QoS 2 and the subscriber must subscribe at QoS 2 for the whole path to be duplicate-free.'

problem: 'The receiver acknowledges, so duplicates can happen' jumps a step: duplicates appear because a lost acknowledgement makes the sender retransmit a message the receiver already got. As written, a student may think the acknowledgement itself creates the duplicate.
fix: 'QoS 1 delivers at least once: the receiver acknowledges with PUBACK. If the PUBACK is lost, the sender resends, so the receiver can get the same message twice.'
